scope_description: The 26 selected theorem statements in BookApplications.lean, their two supporting real-valued definitions, and the exact prose/model passages listed per theorem. This is not a blanket proof of any whole chapter, all exercise subclaims, or all 67 new applications.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem robust_tank_step (x y u w cap sensor inflow : ℝ)
    (hmeasurement : |x-y| ≤ sensor) (hdisturbance : |w| ≤ inflow)
    (hlower : sensor+inflow-y ≤ u)
    (hupper : u ≤ cap-sensor-inflow-y) :
    x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 cap
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Exactly the sufficient two-sided robust next-volume bound in the tank worked route, generalized to symbolic capacity and uncertainty magnitudes.
limits: No explicit nonnegative uncertainty parameters are needed logically: satisfiable absolute-value bounds already force them nonnegative.
The physical affine sampled update, actuator interval, and unit interpretation are not encoded in this one-step implication.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_original_step (x y u w : ℝ)
    (hmeasurement : |x-y| ≤ 1/10) (hdisturbance : |w| ≤ 1/5)
    (hinput : u ∈ Icc (3/10-y) (97/10-y)) :
    x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 10
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Specializes the tank route to sensor error 0.1 litre, inflow 0.2 litre per sample, and capacity 10 litres.
limits: The sufficient input interval is conservative because compatible x is not intersected with known prior safety.
Neither nearest-input projection nor actuator feasibility is part of this statement.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_filter_feasible (y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Icc (-1/10) (101/10)) :
    ∃ u : ℝ, u ∈ Icc (-1) 1 ∧ u ∈ Icc (3/10-y) (97/10-y)
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Establishes nonempty intersection of the safety interval and actuator interval [-1,1] for every valid measurement.
limits: The proof constructs u=max(-1,3/10-y); it does not claim that this input minimizes distance to an arbitrary learned nominal input.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_measurement_feedback (y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Icc (-1/10) (101/10)) :
    ∃ u : ℝ, u ∈ Icc (-1) 1 ∧
      ∀ x w : ℝ, |x-y| ≤ 1/10 → |w| ≤ 1/5 → x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 10
assumptions: The chosen action precedes universal compatible-state and disturbance quantification.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches project P1.B3: for each valid measurement there exists an actuator-admissible input protecting every compatible state and inflow.
limits: The formal compatible state quantifies over all reals with |x-y|<=0.1, which is stronger than the prose restriction x in [0,10].
No probabilistic state-estimation or hardware assertion follows.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_sampled_invariance (x y u w : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hzero : x 0 ∈ Icc 0 10)
    (hmeasurement : ∀ n, |x n-y n| ≤ 1/10)
    (hdisturbance : ∀ n, |w n| ≤ 1/5)
    (hinput : ∀ n, u n ∈ Icc (3/10-y n) (97/10-y n))
    (hupdate : ∀ n, x (n+1) = x n+u n+w n) :
    ∀ n, x n ∈ Icc 0 10
assumptions: Sequences x,y,u,w indexed by all natural-number samples.
Measurement and disturbance bounds hold at every sample.
The sufficient safety input interval is satisfied at every sample.
The exact additive state update holds at every sample.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the tank worked route claim of safe sampled volumes when every selected action satisfies the filter.
limits: All-time input feasibility is an assumption here; it is closed separately by the feedback-recursive theorem.
No continuous-time interpolation or intersample volume statement is made.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_feedback_recursive_invariance (x y w : ℕ → ℝ) (policy : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hzero : x 0 ∈ Icc 0 10)
    (hmeasurement : ∀ n, |x n-y n| ≤ 1/10)
    (hdisturbance : ∀ n, |w n| ≤ 1/5)
    (hpolicy : ∀ measured ∈ Icc (-1/10 : ℝ) (101/10),
      policy measured ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      policy measured ∈ Icc (3/10-measured) (97/10-measured))
    (hupdate : ∀ n, x (n+1) = x n+policy (y n)+w n) :
    ∀ n, x n ∈ Icc 0 10
assumptions: Safe initial x0, per-sample measurement and inflow bounds, and exact sampled update using policy(y_n).
A fixed policy maps every reading in [-0.1,10.1] into both actuator [-1,1] and sufficient safety intervals.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches tank worked route Step 3, including recursive applicability: the induction uses current safety and sensor error to keep y_n inside the policy domain.
limits: Requires a policy satisfying the interval property; the preceding feasibility theorem provides pointwise existence, not a verified implementation of the nominal-action projection.
Uniform sensor/inflow/model validity, not independence, supports the conclusion.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_no_shared_input :
    ¬ ∃ u : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 10,
      ∀ w ∈ Icc (-1/5 : ℝ) (1/5), x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 10
assumptions: No hypotheses: the model constants are fixed in the negated existential.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches P1.B3: the lower boundary with inflow -0.2 requires u>=0.2, while the upper boundary with inflow +0.2 requires u<=-0.2.
limits: It rules out even an unrestricted real constant input, a stronger statement than ruling out one in [-1,1].
It does not rule out measurement-dependent inputs.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tank_large_disturbance_impossible (u : ℝ) (hu : u ≤ 1) :
    ¬ (0+u-6/5 ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 10)
assumptions: The displayed next state fixes true x=0 and disturbance w=-6/5.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches P1.B2 physical impossibility: even exact state knowledge cannot offset a 1.2-litre negative inflow with an actuator whose positive input is at most 1.
limits: Does not encode the separate noisy-measurement interval [1.3-y,8.7-y] or all larger-disturbance exercise arithmetic.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem policy_mix_feasible (p : ℝ) :
    (p ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ mixCost p ≤ 1) ↔ p ∈ Icc 0 (4/9)
assumptions: The left-hand condition includes p in [0,1] and mixCost(p)<=1.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Exactly the Module 8 feasible parameter interval [0,4/9].
limits: The stochastic one-step cost, fixed discount 0.9, expected return and geometric-series reduction to mixCost are not formalized in this file.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem policy_mix_constrained_optimum (p : ℝ) (_hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1)
    (hc : mixCost p ≤ 1) : mixReward p ≤ 100/3
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Universal reward upper bound 100/3 for the displayed feasible one-parameter policy family.
limits: This theorem alone is an upper bound, not attainment; attainment is proved separately.
The policy-domain hypothesis is present although the linear inequality proof only needs the cost bound.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem policy_mix_unique_optimum (p : ℝ) :
    mixReward p = 100/3 ↔ p = 4/9
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Reward equals 100/3 if and only if p=4/9; combined with feasibility and attainment this gives uniqueness in the stated family.
limits: It is an algebraic equivalence over all real p; the name does not by itself encode a constrained optimization object.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem policy_mix_optimum_attained :
    (4/9 : ℝ) ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ mixCost (4/9) = 1 ∧ mixReward (4/9) = 100/3
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Verifies p=4/9 is in [0,1], has cost exactly 1, and reward exactly 100/3.
limits: No pathwise or zero-violation safety conclusion is encoded.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem policy_mix_budget_optimum (budget : ℝ)
    (hb : budget ∈ Icc (1/5 : ℝ) 2) :
    (5*budget-1)/9 ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      mixCost ((5*budget-1)/9) = budget ∧
      ∀ p : ℝ, mixCost p ≤ budget →
        mixReward p ≤ mixReward ((5*budget-1)/9)
assumptions: The reward and cost definitions retain the fixed discount-0.9 summaries.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches Module 8 budget sensitivity and B1: p*=(5*budget-1)/9 is a probability, attains the budget, and dominates every cost-feasible real parameter.
limits: The universal reward comparison is stronger than a comparison restricted to p in [0,1].
Budgets outside [0.2,2], a changed discount, trajectory accounting and uncertain realized costs are not covered.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem policy_mix_flat_lagrangian (p : ℝ) :
    mixReward p-(50/3)*(mixCost p-1) = 100/3
assumptions: Defined linear reward/cost summaries, budget 1 and multiplier 50/3.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the Module 8 explanation that all p yield the same Lagrangian inner value 100/3 at the displayed multiplier.
limits: No global dual minimization, stochastic derivation or policy selection implementation is formalized.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem held_barrier_affine (initial slope horizon t : ℝ)
    (hinitial : 0 ≤ initial) (ht : t ∈ Icc 0 horizon)
    (hterminal : 0 ≤ initial+slope*horizon) :
    0 ≤ initial+slope*t
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Exactly the affine-in-time endpoint argument used to cover every real time in a hold interval.
limits: No explicit nonnegative horizon is required separately because t in [0,horizon] implies it; negative horizons have an empty interval.
This is an order/algebra result, not an ODE or integration theorem.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem held_barrier_clearance (clearance : ℝ → ℝ)
    (initial input disturbance horizon : ℝ) (hinitial : 0 ≤ initial)
    (hterminal : 0 ≤ initial+(input-disturbance)*horizon)
    (hlower : ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) horizon,
      initial+(input-disturbance)*t ≤ clearance t) :
    ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) horizon, 0 ≤ clearance t
assumptions: For every t in the holding interval, actual clearance(t) is at least the displayed affine line.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the Module 10 whole-hold safety implication once the physical velocity model has supplied a lower trajectory bound.
limits: Deriving the line from dot d=u+w, an initial sensor bound, a held input and |w|<=0.1 is explicitly outside this theorem.
Actuator feasibility, scalar-QP projection, delayed measurements and recursive feasibility are not established.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem held_barrier_half_second (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) (1/2)) :
    0 ≤ 3/10+(-1/2-1/10)*t
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Verifies the nominal worked filter line 0.3+(-0.5-0.1)*t stays nonnegative through the half-second hold.
limits: Actual physical clearance still requires the separate model-to-lower-line implication.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem held_barrier_late_counterexample :
    (3/10 : ℝ)+(-1/2-1/10)*1 = -3/10 ∧ (-3/10 : ℝ) < 0
assumptions: Fixed exact rational constants and evaluation at t=1.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the Module 10 one-second clock audit: the same affine line equals -0.3.
limits: A negative lower bound alone does not establish an actual trajectory violation. The prose supplies an allowed constant worst-disturbance trajectory attaining the line, but that integration is not encoded here.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tube_invariant_step (x q error radius allowance : ℝ)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hx : |x| ≤ radius) (he : |error| ≤ allowance)
    (hbudget : q*radius+allowance ≤ radius) :
    |q*x+error| ≤ radius
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the scalar one-step tube and physical-band checks in Module 11 and their altered-error exercises.
limits: q denotes the scalar closed-loop coefficient, not the prose deviation variable q_k.
Negative coefficients require an absolute coefficient variant; the book instantiation q=0.5 meets this theorem.
The error bound, model applicability and unit interpretation are external.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tube_sampled_invariance (x error : ℕ → ℝ) (q radius allowance : ℝ)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hzero : |x 0| ≤ radius)
    (he : ∀ n, |error n| ≤ allowance)
    (hbudget : q*radius+allowance ≤ radius)
    (hupdate : ∀ n, x (n+1) = q*x n+error n) :
    ∀ n, |x n| ≤ radius
assumptions: Nonnegative scalar q, initial |x0|<=radius, uniform error bound, radius-budget inequality and exact recurrence for every natural-number sample.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Induction gives all-sample scalar tube membership under the displayed recurrence.
limits: The sequence-level recurrence and error bounds are hypotheses at all times; local physical-model/error validity must be justified when applying the theorem.
No intersample behavior or limiting convergence is asserted.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tube_thermal_errors (w approximation : ℝ)
    (hw : |w| ≤ 1/20) (ha : |approximation| ≤ 1/50) :
    |w+approximation| ≤ 7/100
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Exactly Module 11 deterministic error budget 0.05+0.02=0.07.
limits: No learned approximation verification, MSE-to-uniform conversion or statistical confidence statement.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tube_thermal_radius (x error : ℝ)
    (hx : |x| ≤ 7/50) (he : |error| ≤ 7/100) :
    |(1/2)*x+error| ≤ 7/50
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Exactly the 0.14-degree invariant radius for coefficient 0.5 and total error at most 0.07.
limits: A one-step sufficient certificate; all-time use additionally invokes recurrence/induction hypotheses.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem tube_error_envelope (x : ℕ → ℝ) (q allowance : ℝ)
    (hq₀ : 0 ≤ q) (hq₁ : q < 1)
    (hstep : ∀ n, |x (n+1)| ≤ q*|x n|+allowance) :
    ∀ n, |x n| ≤ allowance/(1-q)+q^n*(|x 0|-allowance/(1-q))
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the full finite-time Module 11 magnitude bound; allowance=0.07 and q=0.5 give 0.5^n|x0|+0.14(1-0.5^n).
limits: This theorem does not formalize the limit q^n->0, a limsup conclusion, or a persistent-error equilibrium.
For Module 2, applying it to the norm of a vector trajectory requires an external scalar-norm reduction and contraction bound.
Physical applications interpret allowance as nonnegative, although that redundant/conditional assumption is not stated explicitly.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem lipschitz_observation_transfer {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (hf : LipschitzWith L f)
    (x z : X) (observation error radius : ℝ)
    (ho : |observation-f z| ≤ error) (hr : dist x z ≤ radius) :
    observation-error-L*radius ≤ f x
assumptions: Any pseudometric domain X and real-valued f.
A genuine LipschitzWith L f with L nonnegative by its NNReal type.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Exactly the bounded-observation minus Lipschitz-distance lower envelope in the tuning project and bounded-noise safe-optimization chapter.
limits: This is deterministic conditional transfer, not a GP/RKHS, Gaussian noise, adaptive confidence or Lipschitz-constant estimation theorem.
Any physical margin or backup function and its metric must be instantiated and justified separately.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem lipschitz_ball_safety {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (hf : LipschitzWith L f)
    (z : X) (observation error radius threshold : ℝ)
    (ho : |observation-f z| ≤ error)
    (hmargin : threshold ≤ observation-error-L*radius) :
    ∀ x ∈ Metric.closedBall z radius, threshold ≤ f x
assumptions: Same true Lipschitz and deterministic observation assumptions.
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Every point in the closed ball meets the safety threshold; supports the tuning safe-region argument.
limits: No division by L appears, so L=0 is included honestly.
Does not formalize union geometry, query-by-query induction, or experiment reset/transient safety.

theorem_reviews.exact_statement:
theorem lipschitz_implemented_parameter {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (hf : LipschitzWith L f)
    (actual command observed : X) (value error displacement realization threshold : ℝ)
    (ho : |value-f observed| ≤ error)
    (hcommand : dist command observed ≤ displacement)
    (hrealization : dist actual command ≤ realization)
    (hmargin : threshold ≤ value-error-L*(displacement+realization)) :
    threshold ≤ f actual
assumptions: A true nonnegative-L Lipschitz margin and bounded observation error.
The observed lower margin pays for L*(displacement+realization).
theorem_reviews.correspondence: Matches the triangle-inequality implementation-error allowance in Module 4 B2 and the bounded-realization theme in Module 5 B1.
limits: Sufficient pointwise certificate; exact erosion of a union of safe intervals and all multi-constraint numerical endpoints are not proved here.
No actuator error bound, measurement distribution or global safe-search guarantee is established.

coverage_clarifications: All quantified physical data are untyped real numbers or metric points; physical units and empirical model validity remain prose assumptions.
The tank proof covers sampled safety and recursively valid measurement-dependent feedback, not nearest-nominal projection or intersample volume.
The policy proofs assume the defined reward/cost summaries and do not encode their probability-law, discount-series or stochastic-process derivation.
The held-clearance proof assumes its model-to-affine-lower-bound implication; the late negative line is not itself a formal ODE counterexample.
The tube proof verifies scalar invariance and the universal finite-time envelope, not the limit, plant identification or a neural uniform-error certificate.
The metric transfer proofs assume genuine Lipschitz and observation bounds; they do not supply statistical confidence or exact union-erosion/search theorems.
